newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Strong new player seen in German insurance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Strong new player seen in German insurance.

text.p: German insurers face tougher competition after Munich Re revealed plans to fuse its primary insurance units with Victoria Holding AG to create the country's second largest primary insurer after Allianz AG.
News of the merger plans, announced late on Thursday, sent Munich Re's shares surging 10 percent on Friday.
Analysts said this was a good deal giving Munich Re control of Victoria, an insurer which has been attracting foreign interest, without costing a single mark.

Under the plan, which has yet to be approved by shareholders and the German Cartel Office, Munich Re will merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer and DKV units with Victoria into a holding company, ERGO, of which it will have majority control.

Based in Duesseldorf, ERGO Versicherungsgruppe will have total premium income of 21 billion marks ($12 billion), investments exceeding 100 billion marks and annual profit of 380 million marks, based on combined 1996 results.
That will make it the second-largest insurer in Germany behind Allianz, Munich Re's Bavarian neighbour, which last year had global premium income of 74.6 billion marks.

Munich Re currently owns 80 percent of Hamburg-Mannheimer and has an 18 percent direct stake in Victoria, as well as an indirect stake of 5.3 percent. It is expected to own between 55 and 60 percent of the merged group, pending valuations.
"We are not buying anything new, no money is flowing, we are simply bundling existing shareholdings," a spokesman for Munich Re, or Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, said on Friday.
